page.layout: One printed page, text only, no margin notes. Top: running head centred, page number top right. Full-width verse lines at the top, continuing from the previous page. Then the heading "LAT.", a Latin poem of three four-line stanzas. A horizontal rule. Then the heading "XVII. GAL.", a French poem of ten lines. Gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: Car tous les traits du Monde font de cire, Et le bouclier de Vertu est de feu.
main_text.head: LAT.
main_text.p: MUNDUS duello vidimus ut manus Cum præpotenti conferit impares Virtute: si bellum minatur Impavidum gerit illa pectus

p.i: Ultro lacessens: si iaculis petit Vanos retundit firmior impetus. Non, si dolosis usque fallat Artibus innocuam, nocebit.
Virtus repulsa nescia sordida Mundi furores despicit irritos. Ardente tecta umbone Virtus Cerea tela perurit hostis.

main_text.head: XVII. GAL.
main_text.p: QVEL Monstre voy-ie là, qui tant de testes porte, Tant d'oreilles, tant d'yeux, de differente forte: Dont l'habit par deuant est semé de verdure, Et par derriere n'a qu'vne noirceur obscure, Dont les pieds vont glissant sur vne boule rōde Roulant auec le Tēps, qui l'emporte en courât, Et la Mort court apres, ses fleches luy tirant? Je le voy: ie l'ay veu. Qu'estoit-ce dōc?Le mōde.

page.notes: The Latin "Impauidum" is printed with u for a consonant; I have written it "Impavidum" by the u/v rule. The "præ" in "prapotenti" appears to be an æ ligature; I have written it as æ but it could be "pra" in the print. The French "mōde" has a tilde over the o; it reads as an abbreviation of "monde". The top verse lines are the end of a poem begun on the previous page. The small caps "MVNDVS" are set in capitals and are shown as "MUNDUS".
